title: Naturality of the derived-composite isomorphism in the exact functor
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal B$ with enough injectives, and $U:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. Let $T,T':\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be exact functors such that $T(I)$ and $T'(I)$ are $U$-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic] for every injective $I$ of $\mathcal A$, and let $\alpha:T\to T'$ be a natural transformation. For an object $M$ of $\mathcal A$ with injective resolution $M\to I^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], let $R^i(U\alpha)_M:R^i(U\circ T)(M)\to R^i(U\circ T')(M)$ be the map $\mathcal H^i(U(\alpha_{I^\bullet}))$. Then for every $i\geq0$ the canonical isomorphisms $R^i(U\circ T)(M)\cong R^iU(T(M))$ and $R^i(U\circ T')(M)\cong R^iU(T'(M))$ of [lem-sc-ext-derived-composite] carry $R^i(U\alpha)_M$ to $R^iU(\alpha_M)$.
